briefings.title: AI and Inequality: Nobel-Winning Economist Daron Acemoglu on How to Get AI Right
briefings.tldr: Liberal democracy faces a 50-year crisis driven by rising inequality and social silos, but Daron Acemoglu argues that steering AI away from pure automation and toward "pro-worker AI" can restore shared prosperity and human agency.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Liberal democracy faces a 50-year crisis driven by rising inequality and social silos, but Daron Acemoglu argues that steering AI away from pure automation and toward "pro-worker AI" can restore shared prosperity and human agency.

## The Crisis of Liberal Democracy and Its 50-Year Roots
* **Historical Achievement:** Liberal democracy successfully combined individual freedoms with state-provided opportunities, infrastructure, and insurance to create shared prosperity.
* **Transition to Post-Industrial Society:** Over the last 50 years, globalization and digital technologies fundamentally altered the economy, shifting economic power away from workers and severing the link between business expansion and worker wage growth.
* **Geographic and Social Silos:** College-educated professionals in urban hubs like New York, Boston, and London became physically and socially segregated from non-college workers, eroding empathy and creating a deep political divide.
* **Political Realignment:** Working-class voters who historically supported center-left parties (like the U.S. Democrats or British Labour) have shifted toward center-right or hard-right movements due to perceived establishment neglect.

## The Threat of Misdirected Artificial Intelligence
* **The AGI and Superintelligence Trap:** Spending over $1 trillion primarily on foundational models and artificial general intelligence (AGI) threatens to automate vast portions of the workforce, making workers dispensable and vastly increasing inequality.
* **The Algorithmic Cage:** Social media business models based on attention capture and targeted ads use algorithms to police and isolate users into extreme behavioral norms rather than fostering genuine deliberation and bridges.
* **False Dichotomies:** Media narratives framing AI as either boundless prosperity or civilization-destroying killer robots obscure the real debate over the *direction* of technological development.

## Pro-Worker AI and Working-Class Liberalism
* **Working-Class Liberalism:** Acemoglu proposes a new governing philosophy focused on shared prosperity, quality jobs for non-college workers, and community self-government anchored in liberal individual rights.
* **Pro-Worker AI Definition:** Utilizing AI as a versatile information technology that provides real-time, context-relevant data to expand human expertise and problem-solving rather than replacing workers.
* **Human-Complementary Examples:** 
  * **Healthcare:** Empowering nurses to take a greater role in diagnosis, care, and prescribing drugs.
  * **Education:** Enabling a single teacher to approach cost-effective individualized education programs.
  * **Trades:** Equipping electricians and plumbers to handle increasingly complex problems.
* **The Michigan vs. Germany Robot Comparison:** When industrial robots were introduced, Detroit (Ford, GM, Chrysler) laid off workers, whereas Germany retrained operators and welders to become higher-skilled technicians, resulting in superior productivity and lower inequality.

## Economic Levers, Business Models, and Policy Shifts
* **Tax Code Distortions:** Current tax systems in advanced economies heavily penalize labor while subsidizing capital, sending a powerful signal to firms to automate.
* **Business Model Reprioritization:** Business leaders should view workers as assets to make more productive rather than mere costs to cut by 2-5%.
* **Government Intervention:** While governments cannot act as AI entrepreneurs, they can update tax policy, protect data privacy, and incentivize high-quality data investments for pro-worker models.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Probability of Achieving Pro-Worker AI and Liberal Renewal:** Daron Acemoglu estimates the likelihood of society making the necessary investments in both liberal democracy and pro-worker AI at **30 to 40 percent**.
* **Four-Day Workweek Assessment:** Acemoglu views the 4-day workweek as a questionable solution if it is driven by the premise that jobs are permanently disappearing, though he is more sympathetic if it stems from workers gaining wealth and needing time for continuous learning and leisure.
* **AI Agents Prediction:** Acemoglu predicts that humans will **not** universally end up working for AI agents, as AGI will not be achieved anytime soon and humans will continue to control AI systems.

## Notable Quotes
> "If we start sacrificing our institutions, we risk losing all of these things very badly." — Daron Acemoglu

> "There's nothing in the nature of AI that it should do those things. It's how we develop and use these technologies." — Daron Acemoglu

> "AI is going to remake every aspect of our lives. And not just our lives, the lives of six billion people who are outside of the United States and China. They have no voice. And we have a voice." — Daron Acemoglu

briefings.title: Crusoe CEO Chase Lochmiller: Turning Stranded Energy Into Intelligence
briefings.tldr: Chase Lochmiller shares how Crusoe scaled to a $31 billion valuation by building a vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform modeled on oil and gas supermajors.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Chase Lochmiller shares how Crusoe scaled to a $31 billion valuation by building a vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform modeled on oil and gas supermajors. He discusses the realities of CEO evolution, the strategic divestment of their Bitcoin mining business, and managing the operational and community complexities of powering the age of intelligence.

## Scaling a Vertically Integrated AI Infrastructure Platform
- **Comprehensive Scope:** Crusoe spans the entire stack from energy generation and power plants to large-scale AI data centers, manufacturing critical electrical equipment, and operating a managed AI cloud platform.
- **Organizational Complexity:** Managing over 2,000 employees requires deep domain experts across energy, data centers, manufacturing, and AI cloud computing.
- **The Exxon Analogy:** Crusoe models itself after oil and gas supermajors like Exxon and Chevron, categorized into upstream (energy generation), midstream (transport), and downstream (processing/compute), enabling natural resilience and co-opetition across the value chain.

## The Evolution of a Founder CEO
- **The Boiling Frog Syndrome:** Founder CEOs have the benefit of historical context, watching the company grow organically from two co-founders to a large organization rather than feeling paralyzed by sudden scale.
- **Continuous Personal Growth:** Under Crusoe's core value of the "infinite growth loop," Lochmiller emphasized that no leader is a finished product and must continuously invest in themselves.
- **Executive Coaching and Public Speaking:** Lochmiller credited his coach, Shane Metcalfe, with acting as a trusted guide and therapist through personnel challenges, and noted that he had to work exceptionally hard to become a polished public speaker.

## Strategic Pivot: From Bitcoin Mining to AI
- **Energy-First Thesis:** The original business thesis was bringing compute to stranded energy (such as flared natural gas in North Dakota's Bakken oil field) rather than moving energy to market. 
- **Bitcoin as a Flywheel:** Bitcoin mining served as the initial monetization engine to turn stranded energy into cash, creating a profitable foundation.
- **Divestment for Focus:** Crusoe divested its Bitcoin mining business to Nidec (partnering with Ross Stevens and CEO Tejas Shah) to eliminate investor friction around crypto exposure and achieve total focus on category-defining AI infrastructure.

## Energy Innovation and Diversification
- **Voracious Power Demand:** To activate megawatts for intelligence, Crusoe utilizes a diverse energy mix including natural gas, behind-the-wind, solar, batteries, geothermal, and hydropower in Iceland and Norway.
- **Next-Gen Nuclear and Storage:** Partnerships include Blue Energy for ocean-based nuclear and steam turbine technology, Aalo for SMR-powered AI factories at the Idaho National Lab, and long-duration storage companies like Form Energy and Entoura.

## Leadership, Culture, and Crisis Management
- **Startups Die from Suicide:** Rejecting paranoia about competitors, Lochmiller noted that most startups fail from internal execution failures, poor culture, or lack of focus rather than homicide by competitors.
- **Firing Speed:** Acknowledging that leaders almost always fire too slowly, Lochmiller views personnel decisions as complex, snowflake cases where companies scale exponentially while people scale linearly.
- **Community Relations and Marketing:** Facing public pushback and political debate around data center power and water usage, Lochmiller stresses that the industry has a marketing problem and must rely on transparent, first-principled dialogue with local communities.
- **Mountaineering Resilience:** Drawing from his successful 2018 Mount Everest summit (after surviving the 2014 Khumbu Icefall avalanche), Crusoe institutionalized "Think Like a Mountaineer" as a core value emphasizing rigorous planning, preparation, and conscious risk management.

## Notable Quotes
> "Most startups die from suicide, not from homicide. It's not other businesses that kill you. It's you fundamentally not executing on the thing that's in front of you." — Chase Lochmiller

> "We're trying to build an AI supermajor in the same way that Exxon and Chevron are supermajors in the oil and gas industry." — Chase Lochmiller

> "Your job is to be the receiver of bad news very frequently and then be able to think with a clear mind and make decisions in light of that bad news." — Chase Lochmiller

briefings.title: Do You Trust Apple? | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Apple’s new HomeView smart home ecosystem and hardware lineup highlight a fundamental question of consumer trust, balancing the company's strengths in privacy and seamless second-party integrations against historical product abandonments and lagging AI performance.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Apple’s new HomeView smart home ecosystem and hardware lineup highlight a fundamental question of consumer trust, balancing the company's strengths in privacy and seamless second-party integrations against historical product abandonments and lagging AI performance.

## Apple’s Smart Home Vision & The Home Collection
* **The HomeView Product:** 
  * Features a design utilizing an A18 processor and 8GB of memory, with a development timeline that suffered nearly two years of delays due to Apple's AI crisis.
  * Includes use cases such as displaying family calendars and photos (similar to DAKboard), programming thermostats, viewing video doorbells, checking security cameras, and hands-free access in locations like the kitchen.
* **Apple Home Collection Partnerships:** 
  * Designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric for indoor/outdoor cameras, thermostats, temperature sensors, video doorbells, and door locks.
  * **Seamless Setup & Privacy:** Accessories offer one-tap setup with an iPhone via the Apple Home app with no separate app or account required, and are end-to-end encrypted.
  * **Product Availability:** Rollout begins in December, with select accessories launching in early 2027.

## Historical Parallels & The Apple Trust Dividend
* **AirPort Precedent:** 
  * At Macworld New York on July 21, 1999, Steve Jobs introduced AirPort (Wi-Fi), highlighting an 11 megabits per second wireless LAN built in partnership with Lucent Technologies over 18 months.
  * Demonstrated that Apple’s core selling proposition has long been combining modern, easy-to-use technology with strong privacy protection.
* **The Trust Dividend:** 
  * Consumers trust Apple to deliver products that work together without the headache of flaky third-party developer software.
  * Apple provides a strong privacy umbrella, mitigating concerns regarding partners like LG Electronics' sketchy privacy track record.

## Apple’s Trust Deficit & Past Missteps
* **Wireless Router Abandonment:** 
  * Apple disbanded its wireless router team over the past year leading up to 2018 (having not refreshed routers since 2013) to focus on consumer products generating the bulk of its revenue.
  * Left customers in limbo and demonstrated that Apple will abandon integrated infrastructure products if they do not move the financial needle relative to the iPhone.
* **Services Monetization:** 
  * Cameras in the Apple Home Collection require a paid iCloud+ plan for recorded event history, aligning with Apple's push into recurring subscription revenue.
  * Apple Music is natively supported on HomeView, while using Spotify requires a recently unlocked iPhone, which some view as a betrayal of trust.

## The Siri AI Crisis & Competitive Landscape
* **Development Delays:** 
  * HomeView was originally aimed for release as early as the end of 2024, but faced a nearly two-year saga of delays caused by the lack of a working, revamped Siri assistant capable of retrieving personal content and recognizing household members via facial recognition.
* **AI Capabilities & Opportunity Cost:** 
  * The 2026 version of Siri AI is slower and makes more mistakes on basic tasks compared to deterministic older versions, trailing advanced agent alternatives like Muse, Instinct, Dots, and Grok Bot.
  * Committing to HomeView creates a heavy opportunity cost, locking users into a world controlled by Siri AI rather than rival AI systems.

## Tim Cook’s Tenure, The Cook Doctrine, and Future Outlook
* **Leadership Transition & Financial Scale:** 
  * Tim Cook recently stepped down after taking Apple from 1 to $436 billion in revenue and $118 billion in profit.
  * However, critics question whether Cook's focus on revenue and services compromised elements of the Cook Doctrine—which states Apple must "own and control the primary technologies behind the products we make"—noting Apple does not own or control the models underlying Siri.
* **Strategic Partnerships:** 
  * Apple is leaning on partnerships akin to its historical Lucent collaboration, potentially delivering experiences via partnerships with Google and Meta (via Meta Superintelligence Lab).
  * The primary task for incoming leadership under John Ternus is ensuring Apple's "ease-of-use" technology transitions from merely easy to genuinely useful.

briefings.title: Franklin Templeton CEO on SpaceX, Anthropic, Circular Deals & the State of the Market
briefings.tldr: Franklin Templeton CEO Jenny Johnson discusses navigating the current macroeconomic environment, managing late-stage venture investments in companies like SpaceX and Anthropic, and driving internal efficiencies through tokenization and AI agents.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Franklin Templeton CEO Jenny Johnson discusses navigating the current macroeconomic environment, managing late-stage venture investments in companies like SpaceX and Anthropic, and driving internal efficiencies through tokenization and AI agents.

## State of the Market & Macro Environment
* **Inflation and Interest Rates:** Inflation remains sticky and rates are likely to stay higher; while unusual for the past 25 years, historical mortgage and rate levels show this is not unprecedented.
* **Corporate & Consumer Strength:** The US consumer remains strong, with roughly 70% of companies beating projected earnings. 
* **Geopolitical Headwinds:** Persistent conflicts in the Middle East (threatening oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz) and Russia-Ukraine are viewed as "business as usual."
* **US-China Relations:** Characterized as a "frenemy" dynamic where tech domains will diverge, but mutual reliance on rare earths and consumer markets necessitates constructive cooperation.

## AI Bubbles, Hyperscalers, & Infrastructure
* **Exuberance Curves:** Markets repeatedly experience new technology hype cycles—surging to disillusionment before settling to realistic valuations—with AI currently showing frothiness in specific sectors.
* **Financing Horizons:** Long-term financing for power-hungry data centers carries high risk due to the assumption that technology and energy needs will not change over the next 20 to 30 years.
* **Accounting & Revenue Clarity:** Variations in revenue recognition and circular financing among hyperscalers require rigorous active management and caution.
* **Internal Governance Shifts:** Long-term enterprise spending will likely face headwinds as organizations institute governance over agent frequency and route simple queries to open-source or free models rather than costly frontier models.

## Private Markets & Late-Stage Venture Strategy
* **Late-Stage Venture Entry:** Due to companies staying private longer, Franklin Templeton leveraged its Silicon Valley headquarters and venture ecosystem to invest in late-stage deals.
* **Key Portfolio Exposures:** The firm holds late-stage investments in high-profile companies including **SpaceX** and **Anthropic**.
* **SpaceX Assessment:** Praised for diversified strategies (Starlink, data center contracts, and launch cost reductions), though balanced against "key man risk" regarding Elon Musk.

## M&A and Scaling a $1.8T Asset Manager
* **Legg Mason Acquisition ($4.5B):** Closed five days after Johnson became CEO and three weeks before COVID lockdowns; balanced the firm to a 50/50 split between institutional and wealth clients while adding core fixed income and real estate (Clarion Partners).
* **Six-Year M&A Track Record:** Completed 17 acquisitions to broaden capabilities and distribution (including Lexington Partners for secondary private equity and Benefit Street Partners for private credit).
* **Asset Growth Post-Acquisition:** 
  * **Canvas** (direct indexing/OSAM): Grew from **$2.5 billion** to **$30 billion** in 4 years.
  * **Lexington Partners** and **Clarion Partners**: Both more than doubled in assets under management.
  * **Benefit Street Partners (BSP):** Expanded from **$26 billion** to just under **$100 billion** in private credit.
  * **Putnam Investments:** Grew assets from **$136 billion** to over **$220 billion** by leveraging platform access.

## Tokenization & Financial Infrastructure
* **Blockchain Rails:** Blockchain offers a single source of truth, immediate updates, elimination of costly reconciliation, and smart contract automation that will eventually replace legacy mainframe rails.
* **Tokenized Money Market Fund:** Developed the first SEC-approved natively on-chain tokenized money market fund; parallel processing revealed massive cost efficiencies:
  * Lowers account opening minimums from **$500** (traditional) to **$20** (on-chain), with potential to drop to **$5**.
  * Calculates interest every second, enabling atomic settlement, 24/7 trading, and real-time interest payouts for corporate treasurers and hedge funds.

## Enterprise AI & Internal Adoption
* **Sales and Distribution Gains:** Partnered with Microsoft on a multi-agent AI system matching client holdings with product data; yielded a **23% uplift** in client visits and an **11% increase in sales**.
* **Workforce Deployment:** Manages over **1,000 AI agents** supporting more than **800 investment professionals** to handle administrative tasks and code-writing pipelines.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Jenny Johnson** predicts that blockchain rails will ultimately replace traditional financial services infrastructure, though adoption will be slow due to existing toll-taker business models.
* **Jenny Johnson** predicts that long-term financing commitments for data centers carry high risk because they rely on the assumption that chip and energy technology will not change dramatically over the next 20 to 30 years.

## Notable Quotes
> "If you're betting on the needs for energy based on today's technology, both on the manufacturing of chips as well as the production of energy, you're assuming that for the next 20 or 30 years, it doesn't change dramatically. But that's pretty unusual."
> — **Jenny Johnson**

> "I genuinely believe [blockchain] will replace the rails in financial services. It'll be slow because it forces the change of a bunch of business models and the toll takers who who take a fee on a transaction."
> — **Jenny Johnson**

> "There is no person who's had more significant impact, um, on really where we are in the technological advances today, than Elon has."
> — **Jenny Johnson** (comparing Elon Musk to a modern-day Benjamin Franklin)

briefings.title: GTC Berlin 2026: Power Demand, Increasing Grid Reliability and Resiliency
briefings.tldr: European energy leaders from TenneT, Bayernwerk, and Siemens Energy discuss how AI, accelerated computing, and data-driven digital twins are modernizing the power grid, managing massive decentralization, and combating escalating physical and cyber threats as demand surges.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
European energy leaders from TenneT, Bayernwerk, and Siemens Energy discuss how AI, accelerated computing, and data-driven digital twins are modernizing the power grid, managing massive decentralization, and combating escalating physical and cyber threats as demand surges.

## Grid Modernization & The Decentralization Challenge
* **Decentralized Scale:**
  * **Bayernwerk (Egon Wester):** Operates lines and cables going more than 4 times around the world, covering roughly 10% of the German electricity system in the south.
  * **Massive Growth:** Transitioned from ~40 big power plants 15 years ago to more than **1 million renewable generation plants** today, making it the most decentralized energy system in Europe (and home to more residential storage systems than California, despite California having 5 times the area).
* **Transmission Highway:**
  * **TenneT (Catherine):** Operates the largest grid network in Germany, transporting offshore and renewable energy from the North Sea down to the south of the country.
  * **Investment Scale:** Investing **12 billion euros per year** in physical assets and substations; Egon Wester notes his company's current capital plan is **30 billion euros**, heavily weighted toward copper-oriented infrastructure combined with smart technologies.
* **Global Demand Growth:**
  * **Siemens Energy (Adnan):** While regions like Europe (renewables integration) and North America (conventional approach) had different historical journeys, every global market (Indonesia, India, Americas, Europe) now faces identical challenges around massive demand growth (data centers, industrialization, e-mobility) and limited, constrained capacity.

## Security Threats & Hybrid Defense
* **Multidimensional Threats:**
  * **Physical & Cyber Convergence:** Grids face a 3-part threat landscape spanning physical attacks (e.g., severe arson attacks on high-voltage poles in spring), sophisticated cyber threats/social engineering, and personnel safety.
  * **Operational Disruptions:** Egon Wester notes Bayernwerk suffered a cyber attack on a major dispatch center service provider that disconnected them for several months, followed by physical arson attacks on infrastructure.
* **AI-Powered Defense Systems:**
  * **Grid Secure & Drones:** Developed in rapid response with Siemens Energy following the spring attacks, *Grid Secure* is embedded into overhead line equipment to observe surroundings. Bayernwerk also uses drone detection systems with a Bavarian partner.
  * **Holistic Pattern Recognition:** Catherine emphasizes that 100% physical protection of wide-area infrastructure is impossible; AI enables the cross-correlation of physical, cyber, and personal data to detect anomalies, spot early warning patterns, and counter disinformation campaigns.

## Digital Twins & Cross-Industry Tech Transfer
* **Automotive Technology in the Grid:**
  * **Cross-Industry Adaptation:** Siemens Energy leveraged AI libraries from self-driving car perception systems (which detect objects like children jumping into traffic) and embedded them into simulation engines and operational centers to protect critical infrastructure via the **Noedra platform**.
  * **Rapid Prototyping:** The collaborative security solution with Bayernwerk was built within **2 months**.
* **Rigorous Digital Twin Development:**
  * **Cross-Disciplinary Teams:** Building digital twins for transformers required experts from medical science, biochemical science, and weather simulation rather than traditional power systems.
  * **Iterative Success:** Siemens Energy went through **4 failed attempts** before the **5th attempt** successfully created the transformer digital twin, underscoring that energy digital twins require a fundamentally different approach than legacy simulation models.

## Strategic Vision & 2030 Roadmap
* **Autonomous Grid Ambitions:**
  * **Siemens Energy:** Targeting the provision of technology needed to run the grid **highly autonomous (even fully autonomous)** by **2030 and beyond**, anchored by secure hardware and governed AI agents (joining NVIDIA's open agent security platform).
* **Cultural & Operational Transformation:**
  * **TenneT (Catherine):** Emphasizes that every company becoming an AI company requires a cultural mindset shift in a traditional, regulated utility over the next 4 years, alongside upskilling the **6,000 employees** who operate the network.
  * **Bayernwerk (Egon Wester):** Stresses the shift from predictable, planning-oriented operations to real-time operations centered on "Flexiumers" and grid flexibility rather than reserving static capacity for 8,760 hours a year.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Adnan (Siemens Energy):** By **2030**, Siemens Energy aims to provide all technology necessary to operate the electrical grid **highly autonomously, and where possible, autonomously**.

## Notable Quotes
> *"If you want to solve the challenge, you have to really think holistically and not now on one area... the car is a very big example—a self-driving car can detect if a kid is jumping in front of the car, can process this... we need to get these kind of technologies into the grid."* — **Adnan (Siemens Energy)**

> *"We are a regulated energy company, but the tendency that technical possibilities make us more and more capable to introduce automatic decision processes... is there. But the limit is the willing to trust them and the clear responsibility given by the authorities."* — **Egon Wester (Bayernwerk)**

> *"As Jensen said this morning, every company is getting an AI company. I think this is the kind of mindset we have to implement also into a traditional regulated energy company."* — **Catherine (TenneT)**

briefings.title: How an unelected man ruled New York for 30 years
briefings.tldr: Robert Moses and Lyndon Johnson mastered the accumulation and exercise of unelected political power through legislative engineering, control over financial and institutional leverage, and masterclass coalition-building.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Robert Moses and Lyndon Johnson mastered the accumulation and exercise of unelected political power through legislative engineering, control over financial and institutional leverage, and masterclass coalition-building.

## Robert Moses: The Master Builder and Legislative Architect
* **Writing Your Own Authority:** Moses drafted the laws that governed him, notably the Triborough Bridge Authority Act of 1933, embedding obscure subsections that allowed him to perpetually refinance bonds for entirely new corporate purposes.
  * **Constitutional Protections:** By tying his powers directly into bond contracts, Moses made his authority immune to revocation by mayors, governors, or state legislatures under the U.S. Constitution's contract clause.
* **The Hydra Strategy:** Moses held 12 government posts simultaneously—including City Construction Coordinator, Chairman of the State Council of Parks, and Chairman of the State Power Authority—preventing any single elected official from cutting off all his power bases at once.
* **Capital and Speed:** Moses operated with unmatched financial capacity and execution speed, allowing him to deliver massive public works within single election cycles.
  * **Federal Funding Dominance:** By maintaining the largest team of planners and engineers in the country, New York captured **1/7th** of all federal Depression-era work relief funds by **1936**.
  * **Debt Capacity:** In **1946**, the entire New York City government could only borrow **$150 million** before hitting its legal debt limit, whereas Moses's Triborough Authority could borrow **$360 million** in that same year.
* **The YIMBY Graft Machine:** Moses built concentrated private-sector coalitions where banks bought discounted non-competitive bonds, unions secured jobs, connected lawyers collected fees, and party bosses brokered bridge insurance policies, creating a powerful defense network against political interference.

## Lyndon Johnson: The Senate Dominator and Pragmatic Opportunist
* **Transforming the Majority Leadership:** Entering the Senate when the position was considered a thankless, powerless lightning rod, Johnson turned the office into the second most powerful post in America using three core tactics.
* **Leverage and Rule Changes:** Johnson stripped committee assignments away from strict seniority, centralizing control through the party's Steering Committee so he could reward allies and punish defectors.
  * **The Kefauver Defiance:** In **1957**, after Estes Kefauver voted against Johnson on an important motion, a highly coveted open seat on the Foreign Relations Committee was stripped from Kefauver and handed to a junior senator, **John F. Kennedy**.
* **Agenda Setting via Unanimous-Consent:** Johnson normalized the use of unanimous-consent agreements to bypass unlimited Senate debate, fixing debate times and amendment opportunities so every vote was predetermined through off-stage deals.
* **Masterful Coalition Brokerage:** Johnson combined wholly unrelated legislative objectives to pass the Civil Rights Act of **1957**, trading a western federal dam, a jury trial protection for Midwestern railroad union strikers, and federal jury rights for black citizens in exchange for keeping the bill weak enough to avoid a Southern filibuster.

## Ideology vs. Power
* **Moses's Arc from Reform to Addiction:** Moses began as a brilliant young idealist fighting Tammany Hall patronage in the **1910s**, learning that ideals are useless without power, but ultimately became addicted to power for its own sake.
* **Johnson's Opportunistic Pragmatism:** Early in his career, Johnson showed no fixed ideological commitments, molding himself to match the dominant Southern Dixiecrats before leveraging that hard-won power as President to champion the **1964 Civil Rights Act** and the **1965 Voting Rights Act**.

## Notable Quotes
> "Robert Moses was not himself corrupt. He was, in fact, as uninterested in obtaining payoffs for himself as any public servant who ever lived. In the politicians' phrase, he was 'money honest.'"
> — Robert Caro

> "It was not unusual at park and playground opening ceremonies for children, prodded by their parents, to break into the cheer, '2-4-6-8, who do we appreciate? Mr. Moses, Mr. Moses, Mr. Moses!'"
> — Robert Caro

briefings.title: How to Build the Next SpaceX or Tesla
briefings.tldr: The rebuilding of America's industrial base is uniting defense, energy, manufacturing, and robotics under a single wave of American Dynamism, driven by private capital funding physical infrastructure in advance of government demand.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
The rebuilding of America's industrial base is uniting defense, energy, manufacturing, and robotics under a single wave of American Dynamism, driven by private capital funding physical infrastructure in advance of government demand.

## Rebuilding the Industrial Base & The Dual-Use Reality
- **Consequences of Hollowing Out:** Decades of hollowing out the industrial base have created real battlefield consequences for American soldiers and allies, proving that a defense industrial base cannot exist without a robust underlying industrial base.
- **The Convergence of Forces:** A combination of geopolitical conflict, evolving capital markets, and an entrepreneurial base willing to build in hard sectors is driving the current industrial renaissance.
- **End-to-End Lens:** The AD50 list evaluates American Dynamism companies across three distinct pillars: inputs (materials), factories, and end systems.
- **The Dual-Use Model:** While federal demand often acts as the tip of the spear and subsidizes early development costs, these factories and supply chains ultimately serve massive commercial and consumer markets (e.g., Waymo, consumer electronics).
- **The DJI Precedent:** DJI started in consumer drones, expanded into national defense, and transformed into the world's largest producer of robot actuators (the hardest part of building robots), proving how military process knowledge transfers to physical AI.

## Software, AI, and Manufacturing Innovation
- **AI in the Physical World:** While AI is a powerful tool for planning, optimization, and reprogramming, speakers emphasize that "AI cannot turn a wrench yet."
- **Low-Mix, High-Volume vs. High-Mix, Low-Volume:** 
  - Historically, automation required low-mix, high-volume production.
  - Software tools (such as Claude) now empower manufacturing technicians to reconfigure low-volume, high-mix lines in 20 minutes instead of waiting 3 months for a system integrator and spending hundreds of thousands of dollars.
- **Vertical Integration & Design for Manufacturing:** Following the playbook of SpaceX and Tesla, modern founders are vertically integrating where supplier bases are weak and designing for manufacturing from the outset to achieve high-rate production (e.g., facilities built by Anduril, Seronic, Hadrian).
- **Supply Chain Quality Rebound:** 
  - Three years ago, startups threw away 50% of incoming PCB boards due to quality failures.
  - New software-native PCB suppliers in the US now achieve 70% to 90% passing rates.

## Capital Markets, Private Risk, and the Defense "Valley of Death"
- **Private Capital Pre-Funding:** Unlike historical models where companies waited for government contracts, private venture capital, private equity, and major credit firms (like JPMorgan committing trillions to the physical world) are funding physical infrastructure and production *before* government demand is guaranteed.
- **Bypassing the Valley of Death:** Risk capital is helping startups bridge the historic defense "valley of death" by financing capacity ahead of formal requirements.
- **The Capital Advantage:** Unlike China's top-down directed industrial policy, America's bottom-up capital markets follow technological and entrepreneurial success, offering greater flexibility and adaptability.
- **The New Economic Scale:** Physical industries like mining, defense, and energy are no longer just matters of national security—they are now capable of becoming some of the most valuable companies in the world, attracting top-tier engineering talent.

## Co-Engineering and the "Manufacturing Middle"
- **The Legacy Bottleneck:** Traditional OEMs (like Boeing calling Honeywell for a 737 landing gear) rely on 50-year-old subsystems because legacy suppliers are in "receive mode" and lack incentives to innovate.
- **Rise of the Manufacturing Middle:** A new wave of middle-layer supply companies is emerging to co-engineer rethought subcomponents (actuators, switches, valves, power electronics) designed for modern materials and software-native architectures.
- **Grid and Electronics Transformation:** The energy grid is undergoing a step change from static, 1970s mechanical systems to modern, software-native power electronics and battery storage, enabling a complete redesign of the underlying supply chain.

## The Brutal Reality of Physical-World Building
- **Missionary Founders:** Building physical companies requires traveling to remote, off-grid locations, managing tough negotiations, and enduring weeks away from family—undertaken only by deeply passionate, missionary founders.
- **Tangible Community Impact:** Unlike abstract software companies siloed in coastal cities, data centers, power plants, and mines are built in Middle America; long-term success requires bringing local communities along for the economic upside.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Defense Risk Capital Deployment:** Risk dollars entering the defense ecosystem in the first half of 2026 will surpass all of last year combined, which was already multiples of previous years — Connor Love

## Notable Quotes
> "You don't have a defense industrial base without an industrial base, and I think this year really put that into perspective... realizing that the hollowing out of our industrial base that's happened over the last several decades actually has real consequences on the battlefield for soldiers."
> — **Erin Price-Wright**

> "The physical world doesn't care about you, so just be careful in the physical world."
> — **Senior Officer (cited by Connor Love)**

> "The biggest change is, those companies weren't just the most important thing to us, now they can be the most valuable companies. And that's like a big distinction that that has happened."
> — **Connor Love**

> "I don't think that that is a technology problem. I think that that's a... we need to do some soul searching about our will as an American people, and do we want conforming projects to be built, do we want to grow?"
> — **Erin Price-Wright**

briefings.title: Inside Exelon CEO Calvin Butler’s $41 Billion Bet And The Impact on The U.S. Electricity Grid
briefings.tldr: Exelon President and CEO Calvin Butler discusses how the intersection of soaring electricity demand from AI data centers, manufacturing onshoring, and electrification is straining the U.S. power grid, while outlining his long-term capital strategy and community engagement initiatives.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Exelon President and CEO Calvin Butler discusses how the intersection of soaring electricity demand from AI data centers, manufacturing onshoring, and electrification is straining the U.S. power grid, while outlining his long-term capital strategy and community engagement initiatives.

## Business Scale, Capital Strategy, and Financial Performance
* **Company Valuation and Capital Deployment:**
    * **Capital Investment:** Exelon is executing a **$41.7 billion** capital investment plan (up from $38 billion previously), representing a **10% growth** over the last four years.
    * **2026 Spending:** The company plans to invest **$10 billion** in infrastructure this year.
    * **Market Position:** Exelon trades on the Nasdaq under ticker EXC with a **$41 billion** market cap and serves major markets in Chicago, Pennsylvania, Delaware, the District of Columbia, and Maryland.
* **Pure Transmission and Distribution (T&D) Model:**
    * **Regulatory Structure:** Exelon is a pure regulated T&D utility holding company and does not own generation assets.
    * **Financial Impact:** Because it does not own generation, Exelon has not experienced the direct financial boom from data centers that pure generation-owning utilities enjoy.
* **Cost Reduction and Investor Base:**
    * **Efficiency Targets:** Butler has committed to eliminating **$350 million** in costs in **2027**, part of a broader three-year initiative removing **$1 billion** in operational costs to address customer affordability.
    * **Shareholder Metrics:** International investors hold **28%** of Exelon's portfolio, reflecting the company's long-term value strategy.

## Grid Demand, Data Centers, and Reliability
* **Peak Demand Surges:**
    * **ComEd Growth:** ComEd's peak demand reached **23 gigawatts** in 2024 and is projected to exceed **30 gigawatts** by the end of **2030**.
    * **Data Center Scale:** A single large data center consumes **1 gigawatt** of power, equivalent to the output of an entire nuclear reactor.
* **Reliability Rankings:**
    * Exelon operates four utilities ranked among the most reliable in the U.S.: ComEd is #1, Pepco Holdings (DC, Delmarva, Ace) is #2, BGE (Baltimore) is #4, and PECO (Philadelphia) is #7.
* **Rate Cases and Stakeholder Engagement:**
    * **PECO Rate Case Withdrawal:** Following criticism from Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro regarding messaging and lack of pre-work, Exelon pulled its recent rate case to improve upfront stakeholder communication.

## Workforce, Supply Chain Diversity, and Leadership
* **Diversity and Inclusion Spend:**
    * **Supplier Diversity:** Exelon reported **$8 billion** in historical spend with diverse suppliers, including minority-, women-, veteran-, and LGBTQ-certified businesses, maintaining this commitment without federal mandates because "it is good for business."
* **Workforce Evolution:**
    * **Modern Energy Jobs:** Field operations have shifted from climbing poles to utilizing iPads for grid health assessments and piloting drones for line inspections.
* **Leadership Philosophy:**
    * **Cost Decisions:** Butler acknowledges the difficulty of workforce reductions and cost-cutting measures, noting that leaders must make timely decisions to protect the enterprise's long-term health.
    * **Management Mentors:** Butler credits his late mother (a federal government IT worker) for his people skills and his late father (who worked at the Kincaid Power Station) for instilling a relentless work ethic.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Peak Demand Projections:** Calvin Butler predicts that ComEd's peak electricity demand will exceed **30 gigawatts** by the end of **2030**.
* **Cost Reduction Commitments:** Calvin Butler commits to eliminating **$350 million** in operational costs in **2027**.
* **Grid Reliability Warnings:** Calvin Butler warns that if the utility sector continues operating under "status quo" regulatory frameworks without adapting to modern demand growth, U.S. cities risk facing blackouts.

## Notable Quotes
> "If you have great demand, which the data centers are part of that equation, and inadequate supply, you’re going to have high prices... No one cares how reliable you are if they can’t afford to pay the bill." — Calvin Butler

> "It’s like blaming your Uber driver for the price of food. You know, he’s like, 'Hey, I’m delivering it to you.'... But goes back to no one cares. At the end of the day, people are saying, look, this is essential for my quality of life and the bill’s too high." — Calvin Butler

> "We are in a new time frame. We're in a new game and you can't play by the old rules and expect a different result... The grid is letting you know, the warning lights are flashing, but we're not talking about it." — Calvin Butler

briefings.title: Taking on ServiceNow: Coding Agents for the Rest of Us with Serval Co-Founder and CEO Jake Stauch
briefings.channel: No Priors: AI, Machine Learning, Tech, & Startups
briefings.tldr: Serval is a 2.5-year-old enterprise AI platform providing coding agents and guardrails for IT departments to automate internal workflows, directly challenging legacy service management systems like ServiceNow.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Serval is a 2.5-year-old enterprise AI platform providing coding agents and guardrails for IT departments to automate internal workflows, directly challenging legacy service management systems like ServiceNow. Co-founder and CEO Jake Stauch explains that by combining AI-generated code with strict enterprise controls—such as deterministic approvals, staging environments, and audit trails—Serval enables non-engineers across the enterprise to safely build internal software.

## Company Background & Founding Vision
* **Core Product & Mission:** Serval offers enterprise automation and service management through codegen agents, functioning as an AI platform for IT departments to build internal products for HR, finance, legal, and people teams.
* **Origin Story:** 
    * CEO Jake Stauch discovered the pain point while working at Verkada (enterprise physical security products), where IT teams repeatedly named ServiceNow as their most expensive and hated expense.
    * Started 2.5 years ago by Jake Stauch and co-founder Alex in a living room with the deliberate ambition to build the largest enterprise software company of all time and directly replace ServiceNow.
* **Headcount Growth:** Scaled from 20 employees in January to **200 people** today, with hiring velocity expected to increase further.

## Product Architecture & Enterprise Guardrails
* **Code as Automation:** Serval's core insight is that code is the best way to express automation, and AI makes it possible for non-technical users to leverage code rather than painful drag-and-drop workflow builders.
* **The Boundary and Guardrails:** Serval acts as the security layer and ticketing system, allowing enterprises to grant elevated permissions through strict deterministic approval cycles, staging/approval gates, and full audit trails.
* **Catalyst Agent:** An internal management agent built on top of Serval that helps admins and IT pros build underlying automations, configure approval rules, permission checks, and build policies through natural language.
* **Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC):** Unlike consumer agents or unconstrained enterprise AI tools, Serval enforces a traditional engineering SDLC model with dev, staging, and production environments, user acceptance testing, and review gates.

## Go-To-Market & Implementation Strategy
* **Deployment Team:** Serval deploys both a "deployment strategist" and a "deployed software engineer" on-site with customers to map workflows, implement solutions, and manage migration.
* **Pro-Serval:** An ongoing automation engineering service team that embeds with customers after initial deployment to support continuous automation demands.
* **Targeting the C-Suite:** Serval sells top-down to IT leadership and C-levels, pitching the platform as a career-defining move for IT leaders (e.g., Fox Corporation adopted Serval company-wide, and their lead migration engineer won MVP of the entire company).
* **Decentralized Product Development:** Serval has no dedicated product function; instead, engineers are decentralized and immersed in customer Slack channels (with most engineers on at least one customer call per day) to build features iteratively based on real-time feedback.

## Industry Perspectives & The SaaS Landscape
* **Personal vs. Enterprise Agents:** While consumer "personal agents" excel in SMB and mid-market settings, large enterprises require strict permissions and centralized IT control; Stauch predicts enterprise and personal work agents will remain distinct (analogous to corporate vs. personal email).
* **Token Spend and ROI:** While CIOs experienced an initial "token maxing" era followed by pullbacks to measure ROI, long-term spend is projected to rise; Serval prices on workflows run rather than raw tokens to better reflect actual work completed.
* **The "SaaS-pocalypse":** Stauch believes core systems of record (ERP, HRIS, ITSM, CRM) will not disappear because enterprise software maintenance is complex and expensive, but hundreds of smaller point-solution SaaS applications will consolidate into core platforms.

## Notable Quotes
> "Serval is the boundary. Serval is the guardrails. We are the way that a large enterprise with a lot of rules and approvals and process and politics can adopt these tools safely and comfortably at scale." — Jake Stauch

> "Everything has gone exactly according to our very delusional plans. We set out from the beginning to be the largest enterprise software company of all time. We actually made a list of all the companies, we circled ServiceNow and we said we're going to beat them and we're going to build something much bigger." — Jake Stauch

> "IT actually wants to build stuff, and for most of the world, they don't have an engineering department, they have an IT department... We're building essentially the AI platform for them." — Jake Stauch

briefings.title: WHOOP CEO, Will Ahmed: 50B Hours of Health Data, a 4 Million Member Data Moat, & the FDA Fight
briefings.tldr: WHOOP CEO Will Ahmed discusses scaling the fitness wearable company to 4 million members, transitioning to a profitable subscription model, and leveraging over 50 billion hours of continuous physiological data to build AI health coaching tools.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
WHOOP CEO Will Ahmed discusses scaling the fitness wearable company to 4 million members, transitioning to a profitable subscription model, and leveraging over 50 billion hours of continuous physiological data to build AI health coaching tools.

## Company Footprint & Business Model
* **Member Growth:** **Will Ahmed** noted the company took about 12 years to reach 1 million members, another 18 months to hit 2 million, roughly 6 months to 3 million, and expects to end the year around **4 million members**. 
* **Organization Size:** **Will Ahmed** shared that WHOOP now employs **1,200 people**.
* **The Subscription Pivot:** **Will Ahmed** explained that in 2017 WHOOP sold consumers a one-time $500 hardware unit, but observed a "sales problem" despite high engagement. In 2018–2019, they shifted to a recurring subscription model (**$15 to $30 a month**, or roughly a dollar a day) which eliminated device replacement anxiety and changed the company DNA to obsess over user retention, engagement, and long-term hardware-agnostic software improvements.

## Physiological Data, Metrics, & Health Insights
* **The 3 Core Pillars:** **Will Ahmed** outlined WHOOP's primary metrics: **Sleep** (score, consistency, restorative slow-wave and REM sleep), **Recovery** (red, yellow, green dial from 0 to 100%), and **Strain**.
* **Data Scale:** **Will Ahmed** highlighted that members wear WHOOP an average of **23.6 hours a day**, accumulating just over **50 billion hours of continuous physiological data**.
* **Heart Rate Variability (HRV):** **Will Ahmed** explained HRV as the time between successive heartbeats—where higher variability indicates a healthier autonomic nervous system—which serves as a key longevity and stress indicator that naturally drops with age.
* **Acute Health Detection:** **Jason Calacanis** and **Will Ahmed** discussed how baseline monitoring catches anomalous metrics (elevated respiratory rate, skin temperature, and plummeting HRV) days ahead of acute events like COVID-19, lung inflammation, and cancers (Hodgkin lymphoma and testicular cancer).
* **The WHOOP Journal:** **Will Ahmed** noted that **over 50% of members journal daily**, tracking 100+ lifestyle behaviors (alcohol, hydration, travel, nutrition) that generate personalized behavioral insights showing how specific habits (e.g., warm baths, late meals, alcohol) positively or negatively impact recovery scores.

## AI Integration & New Features
* **AI Coach:** **Will Ahmed** reported that about **80% of members** interact with the AI assistant, which utilizes internal foundational models trained on WHOOP's physiological data, advanced labs/blood work, medical records, and member journals.
* **Targeted Health Features:** **Will Ahmed** detailed newly released capabilities, including **ECG monitoring, AFib detection, advanced blood labs, WHOOP Age (health span), and blood pressure insights**.
* **GLP-1 Tracking:** **Will Ahmed** and **Jason Calacanis** discussed WHOOP's dedicated GLP-1 tracking program, designed to combat muscle loss (which accounts for ~50% of weight lost on GLP-1s) by prompting users toward increased protein consumption, hydration, step goals, and strength training.

## Regulatory Landscape & The FDA
* **Blood Pressure Controversy:** **Will Ahmed** addressed WHOOP's clash with the FDA over its unapproved wellness blood pressure feature, noting that despite an initial warning letter and public dispute, WHOOP stood its ground, contributing to updated FDA guidelines recognizing blood pressure wellness applications.
* **FDA Approvals:** **Will Ahmed** noted that while WHOOP utilizes wellness classifications for rapid innovation, it also pursues formal medical clearances for features like its **510(k) FDA-cleared ECG wrist screening**.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Will Ahmed** predicted that WHOOP will end the current year with **4 million members**.

## Notable Quotes
> *"When you're a subscription business, you become really obsessed with your existing members, arguably more so even than the new members. And so it's all about innovation cycles and continuing to rapidly improve the product and obsess over the member experience."* — **Will Ahmed**

> *"One of the principles to founding WHOOP was 24/7 data, and it's why we have a 14-day battery life now, it's why we invented a charger that you slide on to your WHOOP... On average, a WHOOP member wears WHOOP 23.6 hours a day."* — **Will Ahmed**
